name: Chimú (Chimor)
summary: A kingdom on the north coast of Peru, the largest of its period, with the vast adobe capital Chan Chan. It was conquered by the Inca around 1470.

knownFor.label: Chan Chan
knownFor.note: A huge adobe city with walled royal compounds.

knownFor.label: Gold and silver metalwork
knownFor.note: Fine metalwork in gold, silver, copper and tumbaga.

knownFor.label: Spondylus shell trade
knownFor.note: A shell from warm seas, highly valued in the Andes.

location.value: About 1,000 km of the northern Peruvian coast.

terrain.value: Desert coast crossed by short rivers from the Andes, turned into farmland by canals.
terrain.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

climate.value: Very dry, but hit by severe El Niño rains and floods.
climate.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

resources.value: Fish, irrigated crops (maize, beans, cotton) and Spondylus shell from warmer seas.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

disasters.value: El Niño floods, which damaged canals and fields around 1100.
disasters.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

population.value: No reliable estimate; the capital Chan Chan may have had 30,000 or more people.
population.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

urbanisation.value: Chan Chan was one of the largest adobe cities in the world.
urbanisation.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

disease.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

migration.value: Unknown; after the Inca conquest many Chimú craftspeople were moved to Cusco.
migration.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

economicBase.value: Irrigated agriculture (maize, beans, cotton) and fishing, with skilled craft workshops.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

tradeRoutes.value: Coastal trade, including Spondylus shell from Ecuador.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage; labour and goods paid to rulers.
moneyAndTax.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

inequality.value: Kings lived in huge walled compounds (ciudadelas) at Chan Chan; commoners in simple homes.
inequality.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

governmentType.value: Monarchy ruled from walled royal compounds at Chan Chan.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

succession.value: Hereditary, traditionally from the founder Taycanamo.
succession.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

institutions.value: Large irrigation systems linking several river valleys.
institutions.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

stability.value: Little is known in detail; it expanded steadily for about two centuries before the Inca conquest.
stability.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

eliteConflict.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

armyAndTech.value: Unknown in detail; fortresses guarded valleys such as Paramonga.
armyAndTech.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

majorWars.value: Conquered the Sicán culture; conquered by the Inca around 1470.

territoryChange.value: Expanded along the coast, then lost to the Inca.

alliancesRivals.value: Rival of the Inca Empire, which conquered it.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

inventions.value: Large irrigation canals linking several river valleys.
inventions.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

scienceEducation.value: No writing; great skill in irrigation and metalwork.
scienceEducation.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

openness.value: Unknown; it traded along the coast.
openness.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

religion.value: Worshipped the Moon, considered more powerful than the Sun.

languageWriting.value: Quingnam and Mochica were spoken; there was no writing.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

artsArchitecture.value: Monochrome pottery and fine metalwork in gold, silver and copper.

socialStructure.value: Kings, nobles, craft specialists (metalworkers, weavers) and farmers.
socialStructure.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

sharedIdentity.value: Unknown; a legend tells of a founder, Tacaynamo, who came by sea.
sharedIdentity.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

neighbours.value: The Sicán culture (conquered) and the Inca Empire.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

ideasReligions.value: After the conquest, the Inca took Chimú craftsmen to Cusco, spreading their metalworking.
ideasReligions.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

colonisation.value: Conquered by the Inca, who moved Chimú craftsmen to Cusco.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

riseSignals.value: Arose around 900 CE, building on Moche traditions.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

peakPeriod.value: The 14th–15th centuries, when it controlled about 1,000 km of coast.
peakPeriod.source: Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

declineSignals.value: Inca attacks from the 1460s ended in conquest around 1470.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

outcome.value: Conquered by the Inca emperor Topa Inca Yupanqui around 1470.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Chimor (checked 6 Nov 2026); Moseley, The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001)

sources.value: Archaeology and Spanish chronicles. Checked against Wikipedia (“Chimor”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. Known from archaeology and Spanish accounts; ruler dates are uncertain.
